findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` can be bypassed with uppercase characters
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the raw `email` value without normalizing case (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving. On PostgreSQL, string comparisons on `varchar` columns are case-sensitive, and `User` does not downcase `email` before running validations during signup (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly). As a result, a blocked address such as `bad@spammers.org` can bypass the block simply by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

findings.title: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is called twice during signup, double-incrementing `match_count`
findings.body: `User` runs `EmailValidator` on every validation call (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`), and `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which mutates the database by incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at`. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is called when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, followed immediately by `user.save` (which runs validations again). For a blocked email, `should_block?` will execute on `user.valid?` and again on `user.save`, incrementing `match_count` twice for a single signup attempt (and also incrementing it on non-persisting `valid?` checks).
